name: Raymond Castellanos-Pryce
backstory: Raymond grew up in Monterrey, the son of a hardware shop owner who rose at five, wore a tie to the counter and told him that a man is measured by what he builds and who he answers to. He spent thirty years climbing a restaurant-chain hierarchy in Houston and Manchester, following every directive to the letter, and now sells franchise licences from a rented desk in the village because it is a young, growing place where he can still close a deal.
persona: Raymond is a sharp-suited, relentlessly upbeat deal-maker who is sure the next quarter will be the best yet. He keeps his shoes polished, his targets written down and his chain of command respected, and he talks about rank, results and doing things the established way as if they were one idea. He waves off talk of fairness, finding yourself or doing your own thing as sentiment, and has little patience for artists, drifters and anyone who treats a rulebook as optional.
speaking_style: Brisk, formal and confident, with a salesman's rhythm and a habit of saying 'frankly' and 'the numbers speak for themselves'. He addresses people as 'sir' or 'madam' until told otherwise and turns most topics towards results.

voice.description: A man in his mid-sixties. Medium-low, slightly gravelly baritone with a polished, confident timbre. Brisk, even pace with crisp enunciation and a formal, upbeat salesman's manner, warm but authoritative.
voice.reference_line: Good morning. I have three meetings before lunch, and by Friday I expect the new noodle bar licence to be signed and filed.
